record.title: Elekes' tic-tac-toe conjecture for linear 3-uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a **3-uniform linear hypergraph** on $n$ vertices, meaning that every edge has three vertices and any two edges have at most one vertex in common. A **tic-tac-toe** is a collection of six edges intersecting like the rows and columns of a $3\times3$ tic-tac-toe board.

**Elekes' conjecture.** If $H$ contains no tic-tac-toe, then it has $o(n^2)$ edges. Equivalently, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an $n_0=n_0(\varepsilon)$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0$, the number of edges of $H$ is at most $\varepsilon n^2$.

This conjecture was refuted by Gishboliner and Shapira, who constructed 3-uniform hypergraphs with approximately $n^2/16$ edges and no tic-tac-toe.

record.title: Zauner's maximal equiangular tight frame conjecture
record.statement:
For each dimension $m$, let $\rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3$ denote the three quantities defined in the paper, and let $\rho(m)$ be the associated complex projection constant. **Zauner's conjecture.** For every $m\geq 1$,

$$
\lambda_\mathbb{C}(m)=\frac{1}{m}\left(1+(m-1)\sqrt{m+1}\right).
$$

This is equivalent in the paper's framework to the existence of a complex maximal equiangular tight frame in every dimension. The formula is known in the listed dimensions $m\in\{1,\ldots,17,19,24,28,35,48\}$, while the assertion for every dimension remains open.

record.title: The conjectured 123τ–321τ symmetry for alternating involutions
record.statement:
Let $AI_n(\rho)$ denote the set of alternating involutions of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $\rho$. Let $\tau$ be any permutation of $\{4,\ldots,m\}$, where $m\geq 4$. **The 123τ–321τ symmetry conjecture.**

$$
|AI_n(123\tau)|=|AI_n(321\tau)|.
$$

This asserts that replacing the initial pattern 123 by 321 preserves the avoidance enumeration for alternating involutions, for every permitted suffix pattern $\tau$. The supplied text gives no resolution beyond its presentation as a conjecture.

record.title: Andrews–Paule congruence conjectures for $d_2(n)$ modulo 81, 243, and 729
record.statement:
Let $d_2(n)$ denote the number of partitions obtained by adding the links of the $2$-elongated plane partition diamonds of length $n$. For every integer $n\geq0$, the following three congruences are asserted:

**Andrews–Paule's congruences.**

$$
d_2(81n+44)\equiv0\pmod{81},
$$

$$
d_2(81n+j)\equiv0\pmod{243}\quad\text{for }j\in\{8,35,62,71\},
$$

$$
d_2(243n+71)\equiv0\pmod{729}.
$$

These are additional congruences conjectured by Andrews and Paule; the supplied text does not state whether they have been proved or remain open.

record.title: The classification conjecture for essentially 4-edge-connected pseudo 2-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graphs
record.statement: A **pseudo $2$-factor isomorphic** graph is a graph admitting a $2$-factor such that the parity of the number of cycles is the same for all its $2$-factors. A graph is **cubic** if every vertex has degree $3$, and it is **essentially $4$-edge-connected** if it has no non-trivial $3$-edge-cut. Let $G$ be an essentially $4$-edge-connected pseudo $2$-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graph. **The classification conjecture.** $G$ must be $K_{3,3}$, the Heawood graph, or the Pappus graph. This conjecture was refuted when Jan Goedgebeur computationally found a pseudo $2$-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graph on $30$ vertices that is essentially $4$-edge-connected and cyclically $6$-edge-connected.
record.source_name: M. Abreu, M. Funk, D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “A construction for a counterexample to the pseudo 2-factor isomorphic graph conjecture”, arXiv:2207.10961 (2022).

record.title: Class-number ratio conjecture for split primes in imaginary quadratic fields
record.statement:
Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$ be an imaginary quadratic field, and let $C_1$ be the cone whose elements have angle between $\pi/36$ and $2\pi/36$. Let $P_M(-d)$ count primes less than $M$ that split completely in $K$ and whose factors lie in $C_1$, and let $h(-d)$ be the class number. **Imaginary quadratic class-number conjecture.** For two such fields,

$$
\lim_{M\rightarrow\infty}\frac{P_M(-d_1)}{P_M(-d_2)}=\frac{h(-d_2)}{h(-d_1)}.
$$

The paper reports numerical verification for all $d<20$ with primes below $1{,}000^2$, with errors below one percent.

record.title: Cerbai–Claesson–Ferrari bijection conjecture for 201-avoiding ascent sequences
record.statement:
Let $A_n(201)$ be the set of ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $201$, and let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$. A permutation is **$312$-machine sortable** if it can be sorted using two series-connected stacks whose first stack avoids $312$ when read from top to bottom and whose second stack is increasing.

**Cerbai–Claesson–Ferrari conjecture.** For every $n\geq 0$, there is a bijection between $A_n(201)$ and the permutations in $S_n$ that are $312$-machine sortable.

The conjecture is supported by data reported by Cerbai, Claesson, and Ferrari, but the source gives no proof.

record.title: Grassmannian enumeration conjecture for Fishburn pattern classes
record.statement:
Let $F_n(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k)$ denote the set of Fishburn permutations of length $n$ avoiding each listed pattern. A **Grassmannian permutation** is a permutation with at most one descent.

**Grassmannian enumeration conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
|F_n(1324,2143,1423)|=|F_n(1324,2143,3124)|=|F_n(1324,1423,3124)|=2^n-n.
$$

The source notes that $2^n-n$ is also the number of Grassmannian permutations of length $n$, and reports verification for $n\leq 17$; the asserted equalities remain open.

record.title: Fishburn-to-classical pattern enumeration conjecture for 2143 and 3124
record.statement:

**Fishburn–classical enumeration conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
|F_n(2143,3124)|=|S_n(231,4123)|.

record.title: Catalan-convolution conjecture for pairs of Fishburn pattern classes
record.statement:
Let $F_n(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k)$ denote the set of Fishburn permutations of length $n$ avoiding each listed pattern. Let

$$
C_n=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}
$$

be the $n$th Catalan number.

**Catalan-convolution conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
|F_n(2413,2431)|=|F_n(2431,3241)|=\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}C_{n-k}.
$$

The source reports verification for $n\leq 14$ and relates the sequence to known Catalan-binomial-transform interpretations, but does not prove the conjecture.

record.title: Fine-sequence conjecture for indecomposable Fishburn classes
record.statement:
Let $F_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k)$ be the set of indecomposable Fishburn permutations of length $n$ avoiding the listed patterns, and let $S_n(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k)$ be the ordinary pattern-avoiding permutations in $S_n$.

**Fine-sequence conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
|F_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(2413,2431)|=|F_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(2431,3241)|=|S_{n-1}(2413,3412,2143)|.
$$

The source reports verification for $n\leq 15$, identifies the common sequence as A033321, and notes that this conjecture is equivalent to the Catalan-convolution conjecture via the stated generating-function relation; it remains open.
record.source_name: Eric S. Egge, “Pattern-Avoiding Fishburn Permutations and Ascent Sequences”, arXiv:2208.01484 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2008.12297](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12297).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.01484

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

solutions.body:
### Counterexample at n=6 and likely pattern transposition

  The displayed equality is false as written. At $n=6$, exhaustive evaluation of the definitions gives

  $$
  |F_6^{\mathrm{ind}}(2413,2431)|=79
  $$

  and

  $$
  |F_6^{\mathrm{ind}}(2431,3241)|=79,
  $$

  whereas

  $$
  |S_5(2413,3412,2143)|=77.
  $$

  For the first Fishburn class, splitting by first entry $3,4,5,6$ gives the counts $1,6,21,51$, totaling $79$. For the second class, the corresponding counts are $5,9,14,51$, also
  totaling $79$.

  The ordinary count has a short inclusion-exclusion check. Among the 120 permutations in $S_5$, the sets containing $2413$, $3412$, and $2143$ each have size 17. Their pairwise
  intersections have sizes $4,4,0$, and the triple intersection is empty. Hence

  $$
  120-(17+17+17)+(4+4+0)=77.
  $$

  Thus the literal conjecture contains the false equality $79=77$.

  There is strong evidence for a transposition typo. Immediately after Conjecture 10.16, the source identifies the common sequence as OEIS A033321. That OEIS entry lists ordinary
  permutations avoiding

  $$
  2413,\ 3142,\ 2143,
  $$

  not $2413,3412,2143$.

  Replacing $3412$ by $3142$ makes the $S_5$ count equal to 79. All four resulting sequences also agree through the exhaustively checked range $n\leq 7$.

  This refutes the printed statement and identifies a likely correction; it does not prove the corrected equality for every $n$.

  Sources:

  https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.01484

  https://oeis.org/A033321

record.title: Component-count conjecture for $J_{10}^3$ singularities
record.statement:
Let $f_0$ be a real function singularity of type $J_{10}^3$. Consider the discriminant variety in the parameter space of any versal deformation of $f_0$.

**$J_{10}^3$ component conjecture.** The complement of the discriminant variety has exactly 33 distinct components.

The preceding proposition describes 23 virtual components, their involution, and ten additional components obtained by reflection in a vertical mirror. The claim is that these constructions account for all actual components of the discriminant complement; the source also notes that topological-type invariants distinguish all but two pairs.

record.title: Strong optimality conjecture for the Desarguesian ovoid code
record.statement: Let $C_O$ be the code associated with the Desarguesian ovoid in $Q^+(7,q)$, with $q\geq 3$. A code is **strongly optimal** when it is both $P$-optimal and $S$-optimal. **Strong optimality conjecture.** The code $C_O$ is strongly optimal for all $q\geq 3$. The paper proves strong optimality for $q\in\{3,4\}$ and notes that for $q=5$ it would follow from the nonexistence of a linear $[127,8,45]_5$ code, whose existence is open; the conjecture remains open in general.

record.title: Fredi's girth conjecture for the algebraic bipartite graph D(k,q)
record.statement: Let $D(k,q)$ be the algebraic bipartite graph proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko, where $k\geq 2$ and $q=p^m$ is a prime power. **Fredi's conjecture.** $D(k,q)$ has girth $k+5$ for all odd $k$ and all $q\geq 4$. The graph $D(k,q)$ is edge-transitive and has girth at least $k+4$; determining its exact girth is relevant to extremal graph theory and related applications. The conjecture is attributed to Fredi (1995), and its resolution is not specified in the source.

record.title: Conjecture on orbit counts of external lines to the twisted cubic
record.statement: Let $q\equiv\xi\pmod3$, where $\xi\in\\{1,-1,0\\}$. The lines of $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$ are partitioned into orbits under the group action described in the paper, and $\mathrm{En}\Gamma$-lines denote the lines external to the twisted cubic. record.title: Conjecture on orbit counts for square parameters in characteristic three
record.statement:
Let $q=3^{2m}$ with $m\ge1$, so that $q\equiv1\pmod4$. Let $\mathfrak{t}_q$ be the number of triples of lines $\ell_\mu$ belonging to the same orbit, where $\mu$ is a square in $\mathbb{F}_q$. In the computational examples, the number of such triples is

$$
\mathfrak{t}_q=\frac{q-(-1)^m\sqrt q-15}{48}.
$$

**The square-parameter orbit conjecture.** The results of Example 6 should hold for every $m\ge1$; in particular, the corresponding formulas there for the numbers of orbits of length $(q^3-q)/4$ and for $\mathfrak{S}_q$ should hold for all $q=3^{2m}$. The formula was checked computationally for $m=1,\ldots,5$, and no proof or resolution for all $m$ is given in the source.

record.title: The lifting conjecture for transfer systems on athbb{S}\mathrm{L}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)athbb{S}]
record.statement:
Let $G = \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ with $p > 5$, $p \neq 11$, and $p \equiv \pm 3 \mod 8$. Fix an arbitrary transfer system $\mathcal{R}$ on $G$, and let $(\mathcal{R}_D,\mathcal{R}_I,\mathcal{R}_U)$ be the triple obtained from $\mathcal{R}$ as described above. A **lifting conjecture** asserts that $(\mathcal{R}_D,\mathcal{R}_I,\mathcal{R}_U)$ is a split transfer system, and that $\mathcal{R}$ is lifted from this triple using the stated procedure.

This conjecture would provide a constructive method for exploring $N_\infty$ operads for groups that are not lossless, by reducing transfer systems to conjugacy data on the associated subgroup spaces. The source presents this as a speculative method; no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Quaternary bifurcate-chain conjecture
record.statement:
A square-free word is **bifurcate** over an alphabet $\mathcal{A}$ if it has at least one square-free extension at every position. A single-letter extension is obtained by inserting one letter at one position. A quaternary bifurcate word is a bifurcate word over an alphabet of size $4$.

**Quaternary bifurcate-chain conjecture.** There exists an infinite sequence of quaternary bifurcate words $W_1,W_2,\ldots$ such that $W_{i+1}$ is a single-letter extension of $W_i$ for every $i=1,2,\ldots$.

The paper proves a much stronger complete bifurcate-tree property over alphabets of size at least $12$, while the quaternary chain assertion remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Inverse-peak formula for permutations avoiding $2134\cdots m$
record.statement:
Let $m\geq3$ and $n\geq1$. Write $\mathfrak{S}_{n}(2134\cdots m)$ for the permutations of length $n$ avoiding the classical pattern $2134\cdots m$; the **inverse peak number** is the number of peaks in the inverse permutation.

**Inverse-peak enumeration conjecture.** For all $m\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, the number of permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_{n}(2134\cdots m)$ whose inverse has no peaks is

$$
\sum_{j=0}^{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor \frac{n-1}{m-1}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor}(-1)^j\binom{n-(m-2)j-1}{n-(m-1)j-1}2^{n-(m-1)j-1}.
$$

The formula was verified for all $m\leq50$ and $n\leq70$, with its values appearing in OEIS triangle A172119; a proof remains open.

record.title: A mod 32 class-number congruence for quadratic fields of discriminants $-8p$ and $8p$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime such that $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$. Let $h(-8p)$ and $h(8p)$ denote the class numbers associated with the discriminants $-8p$ and $8p$, respectively, and let $\Psi$ be the function used in the paper. **Conjectural congruence.** One has

$$
h(-8p)\equiv h(8p)\left(\frac{\Psi(2\sqrt{2p})}{3}-\frac{\Psi\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{2p}}{2}\right)}{3}\right)\pmod{32}.
$$

The authors report that this stronger congruence holds for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$ with $p\leq1000$, whereas the paper establishes a corresponding congruence modulo $16$. Its validity in general remains open.

record.title: Rado's boundedness conjecture
record.statement:
For a linear equation in $m$ variables, say that it is **$k$-regular** if every $k$-coloring of the positive integers yields a monochromatic solution, and say that it is regular if it is $k$-regular for every positive integer $k$. **Rado's boundedness conjecture.** For all $m\ge1$, there is a number $\Delta(m)$ such that if a linear equation in $m$ variables is $\Delta(m)$-regular, then it is regular.

The conjecture asks whether regularity can be detected using a number of colors depending only on the number of variables. It is known to hold if it holds for homogeneous equations, and the first nontrivial homogeneous three-variable case is established with the bound $24$; the optimality of that bound and the general conjecture remain open.
record.source_name: Yuan Chang, Jesús A. De Loera and William J. Wesley, “Rado Numbers and SAT Computations”, arXiv:2210.03262 (2022).

record.title: Existence conjecture for D-optimal difference families over abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $(v;r,s;\lambda)$ be a D-optimal parameter set, meaning that it is the parameter set of a D-optimal difference family and satisfies the D-optimality conditions. A **difference family** over a group of order $v$ is a pair of subsets of that group whose parameters are $(v;r,s;\lambda)$.

**Existence conjecture.** For each D-optimal parameter set $(v;r,s;\lambda)$ there exists a difference family over some abelian group of order $v$ having these parameters.

D-optimal difference families yield D-optimal matrices, so the conjecture would establish existence of a suitable matrix for every D-optimal parameter set. The source notes that some parameter sets, including $(85;39,34;31)$ and $(99;43,42;36)$, were still unresolved; no resolution of the conjecture is supplied here.

record.title: Cassaigne's two conjectures on the Tribonacci combinatorial-game sequences
record.statement:
Let $(X(n))_{n\geq 0}$ and $(Y(n))_{n\geq 0}$ be the sequences defined by the recursive combinatorial-game construction in the source. **Cassaigne's conjectures.** For every $n\geq 1$, both of the following assertions hold:

1. Either

$$
X(Y(n))=X(n)+Y(n) \quad\text{or}\quad Y(X(n))=X(n)+Y(n).
$$

2.

$$
X(n)+Y(n)-Y(X(n))\in\{0,1,2\}.
$$

The two conjectures were made by Julien Cassaigne in 2022 and are proved in the supplied text using Walnut.
record.source_name: Jeffrey Shallit, “Some Tribonacci Conjectures”, arXiv:2210.03996 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03996

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2022). “This shows that there are infinitely many counterexamples to Rust's conjecture, and one of them is $n = 20$.”

record.title: The solubilizer divisibility conjecture for normalizers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite insoluble group, and let $x\in G$. The **solubilizer** of $x$ is

$$
\operatorname{Sol}_G(x)=\\{g\in G: \langle x,g\rangle\text{ is soluble}\\}.
$$

The cyclic subgroup generated by $x$ is denoted by $\langle x\rangle$, and its normalizer in $G$ by $\mathcal{N}_G(\langle x\rangle)$. **Solubilizer divisibility conjecture.** For every $x\in G$,

$$
|\mathcal{N}_G(\langle x\rangle)|\mid |\operatorname{Sol}_G(x)|.
$$

This conjecture compares the size of the normalizer of the cyclic subgroup generated by an element with the size of its solubilizer. The paper reports computational verification for the relevant groups of order at most $2000$, with the stated exception of order $1920$; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Hamid Mousavi, Mina Poozesh and Yousef Zamani, “The impact of the solubilizer of an element on the structure of a finite group”, arXiv:2210.11564 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11564

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

record.title: Super-base graph conjecture for the graphs $G_{n,k}$
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 5$ with $n\equiv 0,5\pmod 6$ and $k=\lfloor (n+2)/6\rfloor$. Let $G_{n,k}$ be the graph from the paper, and let $\overline{G_{n,k}}\setminus v$ denote the graph obtained by deleting any vertex $v$ from its complement. A minimal prime graph is a graph with the minimal-prime property defined in the paper.

**Super-base graph conjecture.** For every such $n$ and $k$, if $G_{n,k}$ is a minimal prime graph, then $\overline{G_{n,k}}\setminus v$ is not a minimal prime graph for any vertex $v$; consequently, these graphs cannot be generated from any minimal prime graph.

Computations for $n\le 100$ support the claim. It asserts that the indicated minimal prime graphs are super base graphs, meaning that they are not generated from any minimal prime graph.
record.source_name: Ziyu Huang, Thomas Michael Keller, Shane Kissinger, Wen Plotnick and Maya Roma, “On the Generation, Structure, and Symmetries of Minimal Prime Graphs”, arXiv:2210.13680 (2022).

record.title: Laugesen–Polterovich conjecture for the planar convex Neumann eigenvalue
record.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a planar convex domain, let $P(\Omega)$ denote its perimeter, and let $\mu_1(\Omega)$ denote the second Neumann eigenvalue of the Laplacian. **Laugesen–Polterovich conjecture.** For every planar convex domain,

$$
P^2(\Omega)\mu_1(\Omega)\leq 16\pi^2.
$$

Equality is achieved by squares and equilateral triangles. The problem asks for the maximizer of the second Neumann eigenvalue under a perimeter constraint; existence is known among convex sets, but the convex maximizer was not known in general when this conjecture was stated.
record.source_name: Antoine Henrot, Antoine Lemenant and Ilaria Lucardesi, “An isoperimetric problem with two distinct solutions”, arXiv:2210.17225 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17225

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2022). “The question was actually explicitly addressed in an Oberwolfach meeting in 2009 by R. Laugesen and I. Polterovich, , see also , from which we can conjecture the following.”

record.title: Savitskii's minimal-character refinement of Knutson's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For virtual complex characters of strictly positive degree, define a pre-order by

$$
\chi \leq \varphi \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \chi(\mathrm{id})\leq\varphi(\mathrm{id})\ \text{and}\ \bigl(\varphi(g)=0\Longrightarrow\chi(g)=0\bigr)\ \text{for all }g\in G.
$$

A character $\chi$ is **minimal** if $\varphi\leq\chi$ implies $\chi\leq\varphi$ for every character $\varphi$. **Savitskii's refinement.** A character is regular invertible if and only if it is minimal. The refinement is false: the paper presents counterexamples to Savitskii's claim, including an irreducible character of the dicyclic group $\operatorname{Dic}_6$ that is regular invertible but not minimal, and an irreducible character of $D_{12}\rtimes S_3$ that is minimal but not regular invertible.
record.source_name: Diego Martín Duro, “The Knutson Index of the Representation Ring”, arXiv:2211.08123 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.08123

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Congruence conjecture for prime-colored overpartitions
record.statement:
Let $\overline{p}_{-q}(n)$ denote the number of $q$-colored overpartitions of $n$, where $q$ is prime. **Congruence conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$ and primes $q$, one has

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+1) &\equiv 0 \pmod{2},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+2) &\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+3) &\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+4) &\equiv 0 \pmod{2},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+5) &\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+6) &\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{-q}(8n+7) &\equiv 0 \pmod{32}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The conjecture generalizes the proved congruences for $q=5,7,11,$ and $13$ established earlier in the paper, and predicts further congruences for all prime numbers of colors. Its general case remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Manjil P. Saikia, “Some Missed Congruences modulo powers of 2 for t-colored overpartitions”, arXiv:2301.09846 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.09846

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Supercongruence conjecture for the sporadic Apéry-like sequences
record.statement:
Let $A(n)$ be one of the $6+6+3$ known sporadic Apéry-like sequences. For all primes $p\geq 5$ and all positive integers $n,r$, write

$$
A(p^r n)\equiv A(p^{r-1}n)\pmod{p^{\lambda r}}.
$$

Here $\lambda=3$, except for the five sequences $\boldsymbol{B}$, $\boldsymbol{C}$, $\boldsymbol{E}$, $\boldsymbol{F}$, and $s_{18}$, for which $\lambda=2$.

**Supercongruence conjecture.** The displayed congruence holds for every one of the $6+6+3$ known sporadic Apéry-like sequences, with $\lambda$ taking the specified value in each case.

These congruences strengthen the supercongruences predicted by formal group theory. They are known for several Apéry-like sequences, but the assertion for all sporadic sequences remains open.
record.source_name: Armin Straub, “Gessel-Lucas congruences for sporadic sequences”, arXiv:2301.12248 (2023).
record.references:

record.title: The common relative Jacobian conjecture for Type i KSS pairs
record.statement: Let $(A_i,B_i)$, for $i=1,\ldots,12$, be one of the twelve Type $i$ KSS pairs of smooth elliptic Calabi--Yau $3$-folds over $\mathbb{P}^2$, with elliptic fibrations $f_i\colon A_i\to\mathbb{P}^2$ and $g_i\colon B_i\to\mathbb{P}^2$. A relative Jacobian is the relative elliptic fibration associated to an elliptic fibration. **Common relative Jacobian conjecture.** The elliptic fibrations $f_i$ and $g_i$ share the same relative Jacobian $\pi_i\colon J_i\to\mathbb{P}^2$. The paper's abstract states that this claim is proved for every pair, so it is no longer open.
record.source_name: Hayato Morimura, “Totaro–Vial lemma in F-theory”, arXiv:2301.12751 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture for regression depth
record.statement:
Let $1\leq k\leq d$ be integers, and let $A_1,\dots,A_{d-k+1}$ be finite arrangements of hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Assume that

$$
|A_i|=(k+1)(r_i-1)+1
$$

for positive integers $r_i$, for each $i=1,\dots,d-k+1$. A $k$-dimensional subspace $L$, a point $q\in L$, and a partition of each $A_i$ into $r_i$ parts $A_i^{(1)},\dots,A_i^{(r_i)}$ should exist such that

$$
RD(A_i^{(j)},q,L)\geq 1
$$

for every $i=1,\dots,d-k+1$ and $j=1,\dots,r_i$. This is a regression-depth generalization of the center transversal and Tverberg theorems. The corresponding question remains open for finite families of points and was conjectured by Tverberg and Vrećica in 1993.
record.source_name: Patrick Schnider and Pablo Soberón, “Combinatorial Depth Measures for Hyperplane Arrangements”, arXiv:2302.07768 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07768

record.title: Strong well-posedness conjecture for measure-valued drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
record.statement:
Let $b$ be a finite signed measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $H\in(0,1/2)$, and consider the stochastic differential equation

$$
dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt+dB_t^H,
$$

where $B^H$ is fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H$. **Strong well-posedness conjecture.** For every such $b$ and $H$, the equation has a unique strong solution. This conjecture would close the gap in the known strong well-posedness theory for measure-valued drifts: the result is established up to $H<(\sqrt{13}-3)/2$, while the remaining range up to $1/2$ is expected to hold but is described as a very hard challenge.
record.source_name: Oleg Butkovsky, Khoa Lê and Leonid Mytnik, “Stochastic equations with singular drift driven by fractional Brownian motion”, arXiv:2302.11937 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11937

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture
record.statement:
For even $n$, let $Z_n$ be the poset on $n$ elements with relations

$$
v_1 < v_2 > v_3 < v_4 > \ldots > v_{n-3} < v_{n-2} > v_{n-1} < v_n.
$$

A poset is **LE-symmetric** when its Bender–Knuth group acts as the full symmetric group on its set of linear extensions. **The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture.** The zigzag-poset $Z_n$ is LE-symmetric when $n$ is even. This is computationally verified for all even $n\leq 10$, while odd cases such as $Z_5$, $Z_7$, and $Z_9$ provide counterexamples; the even case remains open.
record.source_name: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall, Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki and Janabel Xia, “Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets”, arXiv:2302.12425 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12425

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Non-extendability conjecture for signotopes of even rank
record.statement: Let an $r$-signotope be a signotope of rank $r$, and call it **2-extendable** if every pair of prescribed crossing points can be contained in an extending element of an extension to an $r$-signotope on one additional element. **Even-rank non-extendability conjecture.** For every even rank $r\geq 4$, there is an $r$-signotope which is not $2$-extendable. The theorem proving 2-extendability for every odd rank leaves the even-rank case open; examples are known in ranks $4,6,8,10,12$.
record.source_name: Helena Bergold, Stefan Felsner and Manfred Scheucher, “An extension theorem for signotopes”, arXiv:2303.04079 (2023).

record.title: The graph-monoid equality conjecture for two-vertex directed graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set $x,y$ with adjacency matrix

$$
\begin{pmatrix} A & B\\ C & D\\ \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Assume $A\geq D$, $A,B,C,D>0$, and $(A-C)(B-D)<0$, and let $\mathcal{M}(G)$ denote its graph monoid. **Graph-monoid equality conjecture.** We have $x=y$ in $\mathcal{M}(G)$ if and only if $B=1$, $D=2$, and $(A-C-1)\mid A$. The claim concerns when the two vertex generators become equal in the graph monoid, a relation relevant to the classification of label-regular directed trees up to almost isomorphism. The source reports computational verification for all cases with $A,B,C,D\leq 100$, but no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: Roman Gorazd, “Classification of Label-Regular Directed Trees up to Almost Isomorphism”, arXiv:2303.05673 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.05673

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: Henning's Sweller-start competition-independence conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$. The competition-independence number $I_s(T)$, namely the length of the competition-independence game when Sweller moves first and both players play optimally, satisfies

$$
I_s(T) \geq \frac{3}{7}n.
$$

**Henning's conjecture.** For every tree $T$ of order $n$, $I_s(T) \geq \frac{3}{7}n$. The paper disproves this conjecture by exhibiting arbitrarily large trees for which the Sweller-start game lasts at most $(5n+26)/12$ moves, while proving the general lower bound $I_s(T)\geq(5n+3)/13$.
record.source_name: Jan Petr and Julien Portier, “Bounds for the Competition-Independence game on trees”, arXiv:2303.09993 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09993

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Conjecture on uniform linear growth of twisted Birkhoff sums
record.statement: Let $\alpha$ be an irrational rotation parameter, let $\psi_M(x)=\psi(Mx)$, and define the twisted Birkhoff sum $S_N(\psi_M\phi)$ in the setting of lemma 84. **Uniform twisted-sum conjecture.** Under the conditions of lemma 84, $S_N(\psi_M\phi)=O(N)$ for any fixed $M$, with an implied constant independent of $M$. This asks whether the linear-growth estimate established for certain values of $M$ extends uniformly to every fixed $M$; the source presents it as an open question, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Paul Verschueren, “Diophantine Approximation of Anergodic Birkhoff Sums over Rotations”, arXiv:2304.00635 (2023).

record.title: The prism minimizer conjecture for the Martin invariant of 3-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graph with $2\ell+2\geq8$ vertices. Let $C_{\ell+1}$ be the cycle with $\ell+1$ sides, let $Y_{\ell+1}=K_2\times C_{\ell+1}$ be the corresponding prism graph, and let $\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{[2]})$ denote the Martin invariant of the doubled graph. **Prism minimizer conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^{[2]})\geq\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(Y_{\ell+1}^{[2]}),
$$

with equality only if $G\cong Y_{\ell+1}$. Computations verify the claim through $20$ vertices; the conjecture asserts that the prism remains the unique minimizer for all larger admissible loop numbers.
record.source_name: Erik Panzer and Karen Yeats, “Feynman symmetries of the Martin and c_2 invariants of regular graphs”, arXiv:2304.05299 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05299

record.title: Dimension-boundedness conjecture for cover-planar posets
record.statement:
A poset is **cover-planar** if its cover graph is planar. For a poset $P$, let $\operatorname{se}(P)$ be its standard example number, and let $\dim(P)$ denote its dimension. A class of posets is $\dim$-bounded if there is a function $f$ such that

$$
\dim(P)\leq f(\operatorname{se}(P))
$$

for every poset $P$ in the class.

**Dimension-boundedness conjecture.** The class of cover-planar posets is $\dim$-bounded.

Cover-planar posets can have arbitrarily large dimension, so the conjecture asks whether their dimension is nevertheless controlled by their standard example number. The source traces the conjecture’s first printed reference to an informal comment published in 1992 and does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Jędrzej Hodor and William T. Trotter, “Forcing the Wheel”, arXiv:2304.08112 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08112

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “We close in Section with some remarks on open problems that remain.”

record.title: Corrected Beiter conjecture for ternary cyclotomic heights
record.statement:
For each prime $p$, define

$$
M(p):=\max_{p<q<r\text{ primes}} A(pqr),
$$
\nwhere $A(n)$ is the height of the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n$.

**Corrected Beiter conjecture.** Moree and Gallot proposed that

$$
M(p)\leq \frac{2}{3}p.
$$

This is the corrected weaker form of Beiter's conjecture after the original bound was disproved for all primes $p\geq 11$. The paper presents a proof of this bound, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Branko Juran, Pieter Moree, Adrian Riekert, David Schmitz and Julian Völlmecke, “A proof of the corrected Sister Beiter cyclotomic coefficient conjecture inspired by Zhao and Zhang”, arXiv:2304.09250 (2023).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0910.2770](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.2770), [arXiv:0910.1982](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1982), [arXiv:0712.2365](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.2365).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09250

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2023). “In 2009, this was disproved for every $p\ge 11$ by Yves Gallot and Pieter Moree.”

record.title: Filaseta–Moy conjecture on the Galois groups of the sextic binomial polynomials
record.statement:
Let

$$
P_{n,6}(X)=\binom{n}{0}+\binom{n}{1}X+\cdots+\binom{n}{6}X^6
$$

be the degree-six truncation of the binomial expansion, and let $\mathfrak{S}_6$ denote the full symmetric group on six symbols. **Filaseta–Moy conjecture.** The Galois group of $P_{n,6}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{S}_6$ for all $n\geq 11$. This conjecture refines the result that only $O(\log N)$ values of $n\leq N$ can have a smaller Galois group; numerical computations up to $10^{10}$ suggested that the known exceptional value $n=10$ is the last one.
record.source_name: Benjamin Klahn and Marc Technau, “Galois groups of n0 + n1 X + + n6 X^6”, arXiv:2304.12658 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.12658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

record.title: The irreducibility conjecture for normalized cusp polynomials
record.statement:
Define

$$
P_d(t;q):=
\begin{cases}
\mathit{NH}_d(t;q),&d\text{ even},\\
\mathit{NH}_d(t;q)/(1+q^d t),&d\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

Let $\Phi_r(q)$ denote the cyclotomic polynomial of order $r$. **The normalized cusp-polynomial irreducibility conjecture.** The polynomial $P_d(t;q)$ lies in $\mathbb{Z}[t,q]$, has nonnegative coefficients, and is irreducible or equal to $1$. For every integer $m\ne-1$, $P_d(m;q)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$. Finally,

$$
P_d(-1;q)=I_d(q)\prod_{\substack{1\leq r\leq d\\r\text{ odd}}}\Phi_r(q)^{\left\lfloor\frac{d+r-1}{2r}\right\rfloor},
$$

where $I_d(q)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$.

The factorization pattern was verified computationally for $d\leq 30$ and selected values of $t$, but the general assertions remain open.
record.source_name: Yifeng Huang and Ruofan Jiang, “Punctual Quot schemes and Cohen–Lenstra series of the cusp singularity”, arXiv:2305.06411 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06411

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

record.title: The conjecture on the number of 5-cycles in integer distance graphs
record.statement: Let $T$ be the set of positive integers under consideration in the paper, let $T_1=\{22,58,70,82,142,190,298,330,358,382,478,658,742,862,1222,1978\}$, and let $C_3(t)$ denote the number of 5-cycles in the relevant graph associated with $t$. **The conjecture on 5-cycles.** For all $t\in T\setminus T_1$, $C_3(t)=5$. This conjecture asserts that the exhaustive computation identifying the exceptional values $T_1$ captures every case in which the number of 5-cycles exceeds five; its validity beyond the computational range remains open.

record.title: The $h$-convex drawings conjecture on crossed edges
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 11$. An **$h$-convex drawing** is a simple drawing satisfying the paper's $h$-convexity condition.

**$h$-convex crossed-edges conjecture.** There exists an $h$-convex drawing of $K_n$ in which every edge is crossed.

The conjecture extends the computationally observed examples for $n=11,\ldots,21$. It concerns the existence of convexity-restricted drawings with no uncrossed edge and remains open for all $n\geq 11$.

record.title: Grothendieck limit-shape conjecture for extended parameter range
record.statement: Let $\mathfrak{W}(u)=\mathfrak{W}(u\mid x,y,\beta)$ be the curve obtained from the surface and implicit-curve procedure described immediately beforehand, and consider Grothendieck random partitions with homogeneous parameters from the source. **Extended Grothendieck limit-shape conjecture.** The curve $\mathfrak{W}(u)$ is well-defined for every $\beta<\min(x^{-1},y)$, and it is the limit shape of the corresponding random partitions in the $45^\circ$-rotated coordinate system. This extends the proposed limit-shape description beyond the nonnegative-probability regime; the statement is presented as a conjecture, with no proof or resolution supplied in the source.

record.title: Sharp coefficient bounds for Gregory-starlike functions
record.statement:
Let $f(z)=z+a_{2}z^{2}+a_{3}z^{3}+\cdots$ belong to the class $\mathcal{S}_{G}^{\ast}$. The coefficients $a_n$ are the Taylor coefficients of $f$. **Coefficient-bound conjecture.** The sixth coefficient satisfies

$$
\left\vert a_{6}\right\vert \leq \frac{1}{10},
$$

and, more generally, the sharp inequality

$$
\left\vert a_{n}\right\vert \leq \frac{1}{2(n-1)}
$$

holds for all $n\in\mathbb{N}\backslash\{1\}$. The first five coefficient bounds are established as sharp, while sharpness of the sixth bound and the general inequality remain open questions.
record.source_name: Sercan Kazımoğlu, Erhan Deniz and Hari Mohan Srivastava, “Sharp coefficients bounds for Starlike functions associated with Gregory coefficients”, arXiv:2306.02431 (2023).

record.title: The Desbot-Wilf classification conjecture for patterns in S_4
record.statement:
Let $S_4$ be the set of permutations of length $4$. For a permutation $\tau$, define its descent bottom set by

$$
\operatorname{Desbot}(\tau)=\{\tau(i+1)\mid \tau(i)>\tau(i+1)\}.
$$

Two patterns are **Desbot-Wilf equivalent** if their avoidance classes have the same $\operatorname{Desbot}$-distribution for every permutation length. **The Desbot-Wilf classification conjecture.** The non-singleton $\operatorname{Desbot}$-Wilf equivalence classes in $S_4$ are

$$
\{2134,3412\},\quad \{2314,2413\},\quad \{2143,4312\},
$$

$$
\{1423,1342\},\quad \{3142,3241,4132,4213\}.
$$

This is presented as equivalent to the preceding Destop classification by reverse complement; its general status is unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Alexander Burstein, “Distribution of sets of descent tops and descent bottoms on restricted permutations”, arXiv:2306.08065 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).
